name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_SB2_Q01 - Microbial survival in extreme habitats and colony formation

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Microbes are present even at extreme sites such as deep inside geysers (thermal vents) where the temperature may be as high as 100°C.
Statement II: Microbes like bacteria and many fungi can be grown on nutritive media to form colonies that can be seen with the naked eyes.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Microbes exhibit wide ecological tolerance and can be cultured on laboratory media to form macroscopic colonies.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Two Statements
The first claim is true because microbes inhabit extreme environments including thermal vents up to \(100^\circ\text{C}\), deep soil, thick snow layers, and highly acidic habitats. The second claim is also true because bacteria and many fungi multiply on nutritive media to form visible colonies useful in microbial studies.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_SB2_Q02 - Role of lactic acid bacteria in curd and stomach

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Lactic acid bacteria (LAB) decrease the vitamin B12 content of milk while converting it into curd.
Statement II: Inside the human stomach, LAB promote the multiplication of disease-causing microbes.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Lactic acid bacteria (LAB) such as Lactobacillus are beneficial microbes in both food fermentation and human gastrointestinal health.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Two Statements
The first claim is false because converting milk to curd by LAB improves its nutritional quality by increasing vitamin \(\text{B}_{12}\), not decreasing it. The second claim is also false because in the human stomach, LAB play a beneficial role in checking (inhibiting) disease-causing microbes rather than promoting them.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_SB2_Q03 - Fermentation in dosa dough and Swiss cheese

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: The puffed-up appearance of dough used for making dosa and idli is due to the production of CO2 gas.
Statement II: The large holes in Swiss cheese are produced by the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Microbial \(\text{CO}_2\) production causes leavening in fermented batters and hole formation in certain cheeses, though different microbes are responsible.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Two Statements
The first claim is true because bacterial fermentation of dosa and idli dough produces \(\text{CO}_2\) gas, giving it a puffed-up appearance. The second claim is false because the large holes in Swiss cheese are produced by the bacterium Propionibacterium sharmanii, not the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is correct, whereas the second statement is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_SB2_Q06 - Organic acid producers Aspergillus and Acetobacter

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Aspergillus niger is a bacterium used for the commercial production of acetic acid.
Statement II: Acetobacter aceti is a fungus used for the commercial production of butyric acid.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Industrial organic acids are produced by specific fungal and bacterial species.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Two Statements
The first claim is false because Aspergillus niger is a fungus (not a bacterium) and produces citric acid (not acetic acid). The second claim is also false because Acetobacter aceti is a bacterium (not a fungus) and produces acetic acid (while butyric acid is produced by Clostridium butylicum).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_SB2_Q07 - Industrial uses of lipases and juice clarification

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Lipases are used in detergent formulations and are helpful in removing oily stains from laundry.
Statement II: Market-bought bottled fruit juices are clarified by the use of statins and cyclosporin A.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Microbial enzymes have specific industrial uses in detergents and food processing, distinct from clinical bioactive drugs.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Two Statements
The first claim is true because lipases break down lipids and are used in detergents to remove oily stains. The second claim is false because bottled fruit juices are clarified using pectinases and proteases, whereas statins and cyclosporin A are medical bioactive molecules.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is correct, whereas the second statement is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_SB2_Q08 - Clinical roles of streptokinase and statins

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Streptokinase produced by Streptococcus is used as an immunosuppressive agent in organ-transplant patients.
Statement II: Statins produced by the yeast Monascus purpureus act as blood-cholesterol lowering agents by competitively inhibiting the enzyme responsible for cholesterol synthesis.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Bioactive microbial molecules have highly specific therapeutic targets in cardiovascular and transplant medicine.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Two Statements
The first claim is false because streptokinase is used as a 'clot buster' for removing blood clots in myocardial infarction patients, whereas cyclosporin A is the immunosuppressive agent used in organ-transplant patients. The second claim is true because statins from Monascus purpureus competitively inhibit the cholesterol-synthesising enzyme.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, whereas the second statement is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

Statement I: Primary treatment of sewage involves physical removal of floating debris and grit through sequential filtration and sedimentation.
Statement II: The supernatant in the primary settling tank forms the effluent, which is taken for secondary treatment.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Primary treatment in a sewage treatment plant separates solid particles physically before biological treatment of the liquid effluent.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Two Statements
The first claim is true because primary treatment removes floating debris by sequential filtration and grit (soil and small pebbles) by sedimentation. The second claim is also true because settled solids form primary sludge while the supernatant forms the effluent sent for secondary treatment.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_SB2_Q10 - Flocs in aeration tanks and sludge recycling

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: In the aeration tanks of secondary sewage treatment, anaerobic microbes grow vigorously into mesh-like flocs.
Statement II: A small part of the primary sludge is pumped back into the aeration tank to serve as the inoculum.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Secondary sewage treatment relies on aerobic microbes in aerated tanks and recycling of settled biological flocs.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Two Statements
The first claim is false because pumping air into aeration tanks promotes the vigorous growth of useful aerobic microbes (not anaerobic microbes) into flocs. The second claim is also false because a small part of the activated sludge (not primary sludge) is pumped back into the aeration tank to serve as the inoculum.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) refers to the amount of oxygen that would be consumed if all the organic matter in one litre of water were oxidised by bacteria.
Statement II: The greater the BOD of waste water, the lower is its polluting potential.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
BOD is an indirect measure of oxidisable organic matter present in a water sample.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Two Statements
The first claim is true as it states the exact definition of BOD. The second claim is false because a higher BOD indicates more organic matter and greater oxygen depletion; hence, the greater the BOD of waste water, the more (not lower) is its polluting potential.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is correct, whereas the second statement is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_SB2_Q12 - Anaerobic sludge digesters and river action plans

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: In anaerobic sludge digesters, aerobic bacteria digest the activated sludge and produce pure oxygen gas.
Statement II: The Ministry of Environment and Forests initiated the Ganga Action Plan and Yamuna Action Plan to build sewage treatment plants so that only treated sewage is discharged into rivers.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Anaerobic digestion converts biological sludge into biogas, while national river action plans expand sewage treatment capacity to curb river pollution.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Two Statements
The first claim is false because anaerobic bacteria (not aerobic bacteria) digest the bacteria and fungi in the sludge to produce biogas (methane, hydrogen sulphide, and carbon dioxide), not pure oxygen. The second claim is true because the Ganga and Yamuna Action Plans were initiated by the Ministry of Environment and Forests to build STPs and ensure only treated sewage enters the rivers.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, whereas the second statement is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_SB2_Q13 - Methanogens in cellulosic digestion and cattle rumen

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Methanogens such as Methanobacterium grow anaerobically on cellulosic material to produce large amounts of methane along with CO2 and H2.
Statement II: Methanogens are present in the rumen of cattle where they help in the breakdown of cellulose and play an important role in cattle nutrition.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Methanogens are anaerobic bacteria specialised for breaking down cellulosic material into methane-rich biogas.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Two Statements
The first claim is true because Methanobacterium and other methanogens produce large amounts of \(\text{CH}_4\) along with \(\text{CO}_2\) and \(\text{H}_2\) anaerobically from cellulose. The second claim is also true because these bacteria inhabit the rumen of cattle, aid in cellulose breakdown for cattle nutrition, and enrich cattle dung (gobar).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_SB2_Q14 - Biogas plant operation and Indian development

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: In a biogas plant, the floating cover placed over the slurry keeps sinking downward as gas is produced in the tank.
Statement II: The technology of biogas production in India was developed mainly due to the efforts of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A biogas plant uses a floating gas-holder over digesting dung slurry and was developed in India by agricultural and village-industry research bodies.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Two Statements
The first claim is false because the floating cover keeps rising (not sinking) as biogas is produced by microbial activity. The second claim is also false because biogas technology in India was developed mainly due to the efforts of the Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI) and Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_SB2_Q16 - Free-living nitrogen fixers and Glomus mycorrhiza

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Azospirillum and Azotobacter can fix atmospheric nitrogen only when living symbiotically inside the root nodules of leguminous plants.
Statement II: Many members of the fungal genus Glomus form mycorrhiza, absorbing phosphorus from the soil and imparting resistance to root-borne pathogens as well as tolerance to salinity and drought.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Biofertilisers include both free-living and symbiotic nitrogen-fixing bacteria as well as phosphorus-absorbing mycorrhizal fungi.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Two Statements
The first claim is false because Azospirillum and Azotobacter fix atmospheric nitrogen while free-living in the soil, whereas Rhizobium forms symbiotic root nodules in leguminous plants. The second claim is true because fungi of the genus Glomus form mycorrhizal associations that absorb phosphorus from soil for the plant and provide resistance to root-borne pathogens plus tolerance to salinity and drought.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, whereas the second statement is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
